thread.title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Looking to Extend Rally

title: Stock Market Update: S&P 500 Looking to Extend Rally
text:
S&P 500 Looking to Extend Rally 02-Nov-18 08:00 ET Market is Closed [BRIEFING.COM] S&P futures vs fair value: +19.30. Nasdaq futures vs fair value: +19.30.
Wall Street bulls are alive and running with the S&P 500 futures trading 19 points, or 0.7%, above fair value. The benchmark index will look to extend its rally to a fourth day of trading with the Employment Situation report for October on tap.
This morning will draw attention to the consequential Employment Situation report for October, which will be released at 8:30 AM ET. Particular emphasis will be placed on average hourly earnings (Briefing.com consensus +0.2%), with a strong reading corroborating the Fed's plan to continue hiking interest rates. Also, the Briefing.com consensus expects a nonfarm payrolls increase of 190,000, and an unemployment rate of 3.7%, unchanged from September.
In other economic data, the September Trade Balance report (Briefing.com consensus -$53.4B) will also be released at 8:30 AM ET, and the September Factory Orders report (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) will be released at 10:00 AM ET.
Ahead of the jobs report, U.S. Treasuries have decreased in demand, pushing yields higher across the curve. The Fed-sensitive 2-yr yield is up three basis points to 2.87%, and the 10-yr yield is up two basis points to 3.16%. Also, the U.S. Dollar Index has extended its recent decline with a loss of 0.3%, now at 96.05.
In earnings, Apple (AAPL 210.00, -12.23) is down 5.5% in pre-market trading after issuing somewhat disappointing revenue guidance for the current quarter. The guidance has overshadowed last quarter's better-than-expected earnings and revenues.
Separately, has reportedly asked his cabinet to draft a trade deal between the U.S. and China. The news follows Mr. Trump's upbeat tweet yesterday stating he has had meaningful trade discussions with China's President Xi.
In U.S. Corporate news: Apple (AAPL 210.00, -12.23): -5.5% after lower-than-expected guidance overshadowed better-than-expected earnings and revenues. Starbucks (SBUX 63.70, +5.07): +8.7% after reporting above-consensus earnings. Kraft Heinz (KHC 51.80, -4.40): -7.8% following the company missing earnings expectations.
Reviewing overnight developments: Equity indices in the Asia-Pacific region ended the week on a higher note with markets in China showing notable strength. +2.7%, Japan's Nikkei +2.6%, +4.2%, India's Sensex +1.7%. In economic data: Australia's September Retail Sales +0.2% month-over-month (expected 0.3%; last 0.3%); +0.2% quarter-over-quarter (expected 0.4%; last 1.0%). Q3 PPI +0.8% quarter-over-quarter (expected 0.2%; last 0.3%); +2.1% year-over-year (last 1.5%) Japan's Monetary Base +5.9% year-over-year (expected 6.2%; last 5.9%) In news: China's President Xi said that he and want to expand China-US trade cooperation and that economic contact teams from both countries should strengthen their relationship. Meanwhile, President Trump has reportedly asked his cabinet to draft a trade deal for the two countries. Japan's Prime Minister Shinzo Abe said that postponing next year's sales tax increase would only take place in the event of a global economic crisis or a "huge" natural disaster. Major European indices trade higher across the board with relative strength in Italy's MIB (+1.8%) helping the index erase last week's loss. UK's FTSE +0.9%, France's CAC +1.4%, Germany's DAX +1.6%. In economic data: Eurozone October Manufacturing PMI 52.0 (expected 52.1; last 52.1) Germany's October Manufacturing PMI 52.2 (expected 52.3; last 52.3). September Import Price Index +0.4% month-over-month, as expected (last 0.0%); +4.4% year-over-year (expected 4.6%; last 4.8%) UK's October Construction PMI 53.2 (expected 52.0; last 52.1) France's October Manufacturing PMI 51.2, as expected (last 51.2) and September government budget balance -EUR87.10 billion (last -EUR97.30 billion) Italy's October Manufacturing PMI 49.2 (expected 49.7; last 50.0) Spain's October Manufacturing PMI 51.8 (expected 51.0; last 51.4) Swiss September Retail Sales -2.7% year-over-year (expected -0.2%; last 0.5%) In news: Most large Italian banks have reportedly passed the European Banking Authority's stress test while Banca Carige was described as fragile. On the Brexit front, EU negotiators are reportedly considering a compromise that would not require a customs border along the Irish Sea.
